title: Best Crisp Alternatives
intro: Crisp's day-to-day usability holds up well — 4.5/5 on G2, 4.6/5 on Capterra, reviewers consistently calling the shared inbox intuitive — but its Trustpilot score sits at a rough 1.9/5, driven by a documented pattern of billing and cancellation complaints that the higher-profile review sites don't fully surface. Add a few product-level frustrations on top: a non-trivial number of reviews report message-delivery reliability issues (support replies not reaching customers), and the more substantial features — ticketing, white-labeling, 100+ integrations — are locked behind the $295/mo Plus tier rather than available earlier. In the interest of full disclosure, this site's author has previously written contributed content for Crisp, so treat the framing below as informed rather than neutral on that specific tool, even though every entry is scored against the same public rubric used across this site. If Crisp's Trustpilot pattern or its credit-metered AI automation budget gives you pause, here's where to look next.

entries.blurb: Intercom is the step up in scale and independent review depth — 2,900+ G2 reviews at 4.5/5 for Fin alone, dwarfing Crisp's review base, and a platform built from the ground up around an AI agent (Fin) rather than AI bolted onto a shared inbox. Where Crisp's automation runs on a workspace-level dollar credit pool ($25 of credits, roughly 450 conversations, on the $95/mo Essentials tier), Intercom charges $0.99 per Fin resolution regardless of tier, layered on top of a $29+/seat/mo base — a genuinely different cost shape that scales more predictably at low volume but can outpace Crisp's model fast once resolution counts climb. Intercom pulls ahead on channel depth in one specific way Crisp can't match: native phone support alongside chat, email, WhatsApp, and SMS, useful if voice is part of your support mix. It also offers real compliance depth at the Expert tier ($132/seat/mo) — SSO, identity management, HIPAA support, multibrand messenger — that has no real Crisp equivalent. The trade is cost and complexity: Intercom is explicitly flagged by its own reviewers as expensive relative to budget competitors like Crisp, and per-resolution billing is Intercom's own most-repeated complaint, so you're not switching away from unpredictable pricing so much as changing its shape. Worth the move if you specifically need phone support, enterprise compliance, or a much larger review base backing up AI quality claims; overkill if what actually satisfied you about Crisp was the workspace-level simplicity.

Tidio is the pick if what actually worries you about Crisp is review consistency rather than price — Crisp's G2 (4.5/5) and Capterra (4.6/5) scores are solid but get undercut by a 1.9/5 Trustpilot rating tied to billing complaints, while Tidio holds a tighter, more consistent 4.6-4.7/5 across both G2 (1,900+ reviews) and Capterra (590+ reviews) with no comparable outlier. On AI specifically, Tidio's Lyro agent reportedly resolves around 90% of conversations with minimal hallucination (a 4/5 AI Quality score in our scorecard) versus Crisp's 3/5, where one reviewer's cited 40% query-reduction result is real but capped hard by the credit-metered automation budget on lower tiers. Pricing lands in a similar range — Tidio's Starter is $24.17/mo versus Crisp's Mini at $45/mo — though Tidio splits its AI billing into a separate Lyro add-on (from $32.50/mo) rather than bundling automation credits into the plan the way Crisp does. The channel trade-off cuts against Tidio, though: it covers web chat, email, Instagram DM, and Facebook Messenger, with no native WhatsApp or SMS, while Crisp bundles WhatsApp and SMS into every paid tier — a real gap if WhatsApp is part of how your customers reach you. Tidio has its own pricing-transparency complaints too (roughly 85 of 1,800+ G2 reviews cite unexpected plan upgrades), so it's not a complaint-free alternative, just a differently-shaped one. Good swap if AI resolution quality and review consistency matter more to you than WhatsApp coverage; stay with Crisp (or look at ManyChat below) if WhatsApp and social messaging are core to your support flow.

ManyChat is worth considering only if what you actually valued in Crisp was the Instagram and WhatsApp side rather than the shared-inbox support experience — it specializes specifically in comment-to-DM automation (turning Instagram post, reel, or ad comments directly into DM conversations) and visual flow-building across Instagram, Messenger, and WhatsApp, without Crisp's broader email/ticketing/knowledge-base layer. It's a fundamentally different tool: Crisp is built as a support inbox with AI and social channels attached, while ManyChat is a marketing automation platform with support-adjacent features attached, so this is a lateral move rather than a direct alternative. Pricing has gotten notably worse for ManyChat recently — the March 2026 overhaul cut its free tier from 1,000 contacts down to just 25, and per-contact overage fees ($0.10/contact on Essential, dropping to $0.025/contact on Business) have Reddit threads describing bills growing 2-3x as lists scale, a sharper contrast to Crisp's still-usable 2-seat free tier and workspace-based (not contact-based) pricing. ManyChat's own Pricing Value score in our scorecard (2/5) is the lowest of any tool compared here, well below Crisp's 4/5. What ManyChat does better than Crisp, unambiguously, is Instagram-specific growth mechanics — comment-to-DM, Story mention triggers, keyword triggers — none of which Crisp attempts to replicate. Only make this switch if Instagram-led lead generation is genuinely your primary use case and you're comfortable managing contact-count exposure; if you need a real support inbox, Crisp remains the better-shaped tool of the two.
